$comment: Corporate.md §9 — the perishable half of the module, deliberately a data file rather than spec prose so the spec does not rot on harness release cadence. THREE RULES govern this file: (1) a row requires a source — any flag, key, or path not confirmed verbatim against vendor documentation belongs in `caveats`, never in `harnesses`, because a plausible-looking flag is worse than a gap: it will be pasted into a launcher; (2) bind per invocation, never by a global pin — a pin can silently override an explicit per-seat choice, so the resolved value must travel with the invocation and actual application must be observed rather than assumed; (3) this file states its own expiry — `revisit` makes re-survey scheduled rather than reactive, and the `watch` seat (§3.2) is its executor.

revisit.reason: Agent CLIs ship flag changes on a weeks-to-months cadence. Past the date a verify axis reports a reminder; past the grace it fails. Re-survey updates asOf, revisit, and watchlist together.

fields.$comment: The field contract every confirmed row must satisfy. A row missing a required field is not a partial row — it is a caveat.
fields.harness: stable identifier used by roster `harness` values
fields.label: human-facing name
fields.instructionFile: the per-directory instruction filename this harness discovers (Corporate.md §2.2)
fields.instructionOrder: the discovery/merge order, stated as observed — Corporate.md §2.2 depends on knowing this rather than assuming it
fields.instructionImport: the syntax, if any, by which an instruction file includes another — null when the harness has none, in which case the charter must instruct the agent to read the project SSoT
fields.nonInteractive: how to run one turn without a TTY
fields.sessionContinue: how to continue the same conversation across invocations (§7.1 residency depends on this)
fields.sessionStore: where session transcripts live — needed to reason about desk locality and cleanup
fields.pathGrant: how to grant read/write beyond the working directory (§2.3) — enumerated, never blanket
fields.effortBind: per-invocation reasoning-effort selection, where the harness exposes one; null when it does not
fields.budgetBind: per-invocation turn/spend ceilings, where the harness exposes them (§7.4b prefers these over module-side accounting)
fields.selfConfigProtection: whether the harness itself prevents an agent from editing its own configuration (§9.2)
fields.customEndpoint: how to point the harness at a non-default endpoint (§9.1) — mechanism only; permission is the deployment's responsibility
fields.gotchas: behaviours that break a naive desk/residency implementation
fields.confirmedBy: REQUIRED — source URL(s) where the strings above were read verbatim
fields.confirmedOn: REQUIRED — date the source was read
fields.providerBind: How (and whether) the harness can be pointed at a model endpoint other than its vendor default. Decides which seats an external or local API can staff at all, and at what config scope the choice lives — a scope narrower than the seat means the seat cannot carry its own provider.

harnesses.label: Claude Code CLI
harnesses.instructionOrder: Collected by walking upward from cwd, then concatenated filesystem-root → cwd (append, not overwrite). A subdirectory CLAUDE.md is loaded on demand when a file in that directory is read, not at launch. Scope order: managed policy → user ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md → project → local.
harnesses.instructionImport: @path/to/file — up to 4 recursive hops; relative paths resolve against the importing file; a path inside backticks is literal. AGENTS.md is NOT read natively; the documented bridge is an `@AGENTS.md` import from CLAUDE.md.
harnesses.pathScopedRules: .claude/rules/*.md with optional `paths` glob frontmatter (recursive discovery; user-level ~/.claude/rules/ loads before project rules so project wins).
harnesses.nonInteractive: -p / --print (every CLI option works alongside it); stdin may be piped in
harnesses.sessionContinue: --continue (-c) resumes the newest conversation in the current directory; or capture the id from `--output-format json` and pass `--resume <session-id>`. Both invocations MUST run in the same directory — session lookup is scoped to the project directory and its git worktrees.
harnesses.sessionStore: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, where <project> is the working-directory path with non-alphanumerics replaced by '-'. Relocate with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR; retention via cleanupPeriodDays; suppress a one-shot with --no-session-persistence. The entry format is documented as internal and version-unstable — do not parse it.
harnesses.memoryStore: ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ with MEMORY.md as the index. Only the first 200 lines or 25 KB of MEMORY.md (whichever comes first) is loaded at session start. <project> derives from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories share one memory directory.
harnesses.pathGrant: --add-dir <path> (repeatable) or /add-dir in session; permanently via settings permissions.additionalDirectories
harnesses.budgetBind: --max-budget-usd <amount>. NOTE: --max-turns is NOT present in the binary measured on this deployment (2026-07-25) although it appears in some documentation — a CORRECTED row, and exactly the class of drift rule 1 exists to keep out of a launcher. Bind spend, not turns, until a build is measured that carries it.
harnesses.selfConfigProtection: none at the harness level — Corporate.md §9.2's no-self-configuration invariant must be carried by the charter and the path grant here
gotchas: PATH-GRANT ASYMMETRY (affects desks directly): directories added with --add-dir / /add-dir also load that directory's .claude/skills/, .claude/agents/ and the enabledPlugins + extraKnownMarketplaces settings keys. Directories listed in permissions.additionalDirectories grant FILE ACCESS ONLY and load no configuration. Choose deliberately: a desk that needs the project's skills must use --add-dir, not the settings key.

RESUME DOES NOT RESTORE: --mcp-config, --settings, --plugin-dir, --fallback-model, and --add-dir must be passed again on every resume. The plan and bypassPermissions permission modes are never restored. settings.json / settings.local.json ARE re-read each launch. A resident seat's launcher must therefore keep its full flag set, not just the session id.
A session created by -p does not appear in the interactive --resume picker; it is resumable only by explicit session id.

CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 is set in subprocesses the harness spawns, and such nested sessions are excluded from --resume/--continue/history; CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE overrides that exclusion. A supervisor spawning seats from inside a session must know which behaviour it wants.

--bare skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md, restricts tools to Bash/read/edit, and skips OAuth/keychain (so it needs an API key or an apiKeyHelper). Documented as the recommended mode for scripted calls — but it defeats the charter-discovery mechanism §2.2 relies on, so a Corporate desk using --bare must inject its charter explicitly.

A background-agent supervisor exists in-product (--bg plus `claude agents`), so a residency implementation should evaluate it before building a bespoke supervisor — §13 already names the bespoke supervisor a prunable unit for exactly this reason.
confirmedBy: local measurement: claude.exe --help and claude.exe agents --help on the deployment host, 2026-07-25
harnesses.backgroundMode: --bg / --background starts the session as a background agent and returns immediately; `claude agents` manages the resulting sessions (its own flag set includes --add-dir, --agent, --effort, --cwd, --all, --json). The OS-service installation path around this remains undocumented — that gap is a Corporate contribution target, not a registry fact.
harnesses.providerBind: Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings (OAuth and keychain are never read in print mode); third-party providers are Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry, each with their own credentials. There is NO arbitrary OpenAI-compatible base_url: reaching one needs a shim that speaks the Anthropic wire, which puts the shim host inside the credential blast radius (Corporate §9.2) — so an arbitrary external endpoint is not a way to staff a claude-code seat, and the honest options are the operator subscription, an Anthropic key, or one of the three named clouds. MEASURED here 2026-07-26 (--help on the installed binary).

harnesses.label: OpenAI Codex CLI
harnesses.instructionFile: AGENTS.override.md, else AGENTS.md, else project_doc_fallback_filenames — at most ONE file per directory
harnesses.instructionOrder: Global scope first (CODEX_HOME, default ~/.codex: AGENTS.override.md then AGENTS.md — one file), then project scope walking project root → cwd, concatenated root-first with blank-line separators. The file nearest cwd therefore lands LAST and wins. Empty files are skipped; accumulation stops at project_doc_max_bytes (default 32 KiB). The chain is built once per run.
harnesses.nonInteractive: codex exec (alias codex e); `cat prompt.txt | codex exec -` uses stdin as the prompt
harnesses.sessionContinue: codex exec resume --last "<prompt>" or codex exec resume <SESSION_ID> (--all searches all directories); interactive: codex resume [--last]
harnesses.sessionStore: ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-YYYY-MM-DDThh-mm-ss-<uuid>.jsonl (a .jsonl.zst variant is recognised); --ephemeral skips persisting rollout files
harnesses.configFiles: Precedence: CLI flags and -c/--config overrides → project .codex/config.toml (nearest wins, trusted projects only) → profile ~/.codex/<name>.config.toml (--profile) → user ~/.codex/config.toml → system /etc/codex/config.toml → built-in defaults. Local state root is CODEX_HOME (default ~/.codex). TOML constraint: root keys must precede tables.
harnesses.pathGrant: sandbox_mode = "workspace-write" plus [sandbox_workspace_write].writable_roots (array); companions network_access, exclude_tmpdir_env_var, exclude_slash_tmp. Full release is sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access" or --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox.
harnesses.sandboxFlags: --sandbox|-s read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access · --ask-for-approval|-a untrusted|on-request|never · --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (alias --yolo). codex exec defaults to the read-only sandbox. --full-auto is deprecated in favour of --sandbox workspace-write.
harnesses.effortBind: config key model_reasoning_effort = minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh (xhigh depends on model support)
harnesses.trust: projects.<path>.trust_level = "trusted"|"untrusted". An untrusted project skips the entire project-scoped .codex/ layer (project config, hooks, rules) and loads only user/system config.
harnesses.selfConfigProtection: ENFORCED BY THE HARNESS: inside writable roots, .git (including the real path behind a gitdir pointer), .agents (when present as a directory) and .codex (when present as a directory) remain read-only. This is the vendor-level precedent Corporate.md §9.2 generalizes into a cross-harness invariant.
harnesses.customEndpoint: config.toml model_providers table (see caveats — the exact key set was not confirmed verbatim in this survey)
harnesses.outputFlags: -o/--output-last-message <path> · --json (alias --experimental-json) · --output-schema <path> (final response conforms to a JSON Schema) · --ignore-user-config · --ignore-rules · --cd/-C <path> · --skip-git-repo-check
gotchas: A project must be trusted for its .codex/ layer to load at all — so a desk relying on project-local config silently loses it when the trust entry is missing. The scriptable path for granting trust in a non-interactive run was NOT confirmed (see caveats).
Auth injection is documented inline (CODEX_API_KEY=<key> codex exec ...) rather than as job-level environment, which matters for a supervisor spawning many seats.

`codex doctor` diagnoses install, config, auth and runtime health — the natural liveness probe for a supervisor to run before declaring a seat available, instead of inferring health from a failed turn.
confirmedBy: local measurement: codex.exe --help and codex.exe exec --help on the deployment host, 2026-07-25
harnesses.subcommands: exec (alias e) · review · resume / archive / delete / unarchive (session lifecycle) · login / logout · mcp / mcp-server · plugin · app-server · remote-control · app · sandbox (run a command inside the Codex sandbox) · doctor (diagnose install, config, auth, runtime health) · update · completion · debug · apply (alias a)
harnesses.configOverride: -c / --config key=value with dotted paths for nested values; the value is parsed as TOML and falls back to a literal string if it does not parse. Confirmed: `-c model="o3"`, `-c 'sandbox_permissions=["disk-full-read-access"]'`, `-c shell_environment_policy.inherit=all`.
harnesses.stdinContract: A bare PROMPT argument, or `-` to read from stdin. If stdin is piped AND a prompt argument is given, stdin is appended as a <stdin> block — so a supervisor can pass a charter as the argument and the inbound as the pipe without them colliding.
harnesses.providerBind: Custom providers are declared as [model_providers.<id>] with name / base_url / env_key / wire_api, and the model_provider key selects one. Three constraints decide whether a seat can use this: (1) wire_api MUST be "responses" — chat/completions was deprecated 2026-02 and a custom provider with wire_api="chat" or with the field absent fails at startup, so an endpoint that only speaks chat/completions cannot back a codex seat at all; (2) the built-in ids openai / ollama / lmstudio are reserved and the openai base_url cannot be overridden, so an alternative vendor must be a new provider id; (3) model_provider and model_providers are honored only in the USER-level ~/.codex/config.toml and are ignored in a project-local .codex/config.toml with a startup warning — therefore a Corporate desk cannot carry its seat provider, and per-seat variation goes through profiles (-p <name>, layering $CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml) instead. Local models are first-class and need none of this: --oss with --local-provider lmstudio|ollama. Flags MEASURED here 2026-07-26 (--oss / --local-provider / -c / --profile / --strict-config present); the config-key semantics are WEB-SOURCED 2026-07-26 and not verified against a live custom provider on this deployment.

harnesses.label: Google Antigravity CLI
harnesses.identity: Antigravity CLI, invoked as `agy`. Official docs at antigravity.google/docs/cli/*; official repo google-antigravity/antigravity-cli carries README/CHANGELOG/examples only — the binary is distributed, not the source. Shares the core agent engine and bidirectional settings sync with the Antigravity GUI.
harnesses.instructionFile: GEMINI.md and AGENTS.md in the active directory; global constraints from ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md
harnesses.instructionOrder: Global then active-directory, per the Gemini CLI lineage it inherits (see gotchas — a full per-directory merge order was not confirmed for this CLI specifically).
harnesses.nonInteractive: -p / --print (--prompt is an ALIAS for --print, not a separate flag); -i / --prompt-interactive runs a prompt then stays interactive
harnesses.sessionContinue: -c / --continue (confirmed: -c is the alias of --continue) resumes the most recent conversation; --conversation <id> resumes a specific one. There is no fork/new-session-id flag.
harnesses.sessionStore: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/cache/last_conversations.json maps absolute workspace paths to their most recently active conversation id; workspace↔project mapping in cache/projects.json. Conversation history is scoped to the current working directory.
harnesses.configFiles: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json (keybindings in the sibling keybindings.json). Extension paths moved from the Gemini CLI layout: global skills ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills/, workspace skills .agents/skills/, global MCP ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, workspace MCP .agents/mcp_config.json (schema key url/httpUrl → serverUrl), workspace hooks <workspace>/.agents/hooks.json.
harnesses.pathGrant: settings.json allowNonWorkspaceAccess (DEFAULT off) plus /add-dir <path> in session; permission rules live in the same settings.json under `permissions` as allow/deny/ask lists with precedence Deny > Ask > Allow (rule syntax e.g. "command(git)"), managed in session via /permissions
harnesses.modelBind: --model <slug> — in print mode an unresolvable slug is a hard non-zero failure that prints the available model list; interactive warns and falls back
harnesses.effortBind: --effort low|medium|high (three values only — a narrower ladder than the other harnesses)
harnesses.selfConfigProtection: not documented as harness-enforced; the .agents/ convention is shared with Codex (which does protect it), so a deployment should assume it must enforce §9.2 itself
gotchas: Print mode has a wall-clock ceiling of its own: --print-timeout, default 5m0s. A seat whose turn can exceed five minutes must raise it explicitly or it is silently cut.

No structured output. Where the other harnesses can return JSON, agy returns prose — so a seat on agy should be one whose product is judgement for a human or another model to read, not a record to be parsed. This is why the reviewer seat fits it and a scribe seat does not.

Headless runs honour persisted settings.json policies, and a tool needing confirmation is soft-denied with a stderr notice naming the required allow-rule. Parse that notice; treating silence as success is the failure it was fixed to prevent.
allowNonWorkspaceAccess defaults to off, so a desk needs an explicit grant before it can read the project root.
harnesses.install: macOS/Linux: curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash · Windows PowerShell: irm https://antigravity.google/cli/install.ps1 | iex
confirmedBy: local measurement: agy.exe --version (1.1.7) and agy.exe --help on the deployment host, 2026-07-25
harnesses.subcommands: agent/agents (list) · models (list) · plugin/plugins · changelog · update · install ("Configure environment paths and shell settings" — this is what writes the PATH entry) · help
harnesses.outputFormat: NONE — print mode emits plain text. There is no --output-format or --json, so a supervisor parses prose or nothing. This is the sharpest constraint on using agy for a machine-consumed seat.
harnesses.provenance: docs + official changelog, then CONFIRMED against the installed binary on the deployment host
harnesses.providerBind: No provider or base-url surface in --help on this deployment (2026-07-26): the only model-facing entries are --model and a models subcommand. Treat as subscription-bound — an external endpoint cannot staff an agy seat until a provider surface is measured, and absence in --help is not proof of absence in the binary, only of absence in its documented surface.

harnesses.label: Gemini CLI
harnesses.status: SUPERSEDED FOR CONSUMER PLANS — read `entitlementChange` before assigning a seat
harnesses.entitlementChange: As announced 2026-06-18, Gemini CLI and the Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions stopped serving requests for Google AI Pro and Ultra (free tier included); Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licences are stated to be unaffected. A seat backed by a consumer Google subscription therefore belongs on `agy` (Antigravity CLI), not here. Note the documentation/reality mismatch recorded in watchlist.
harnesses.instructionFile: GEMINI.md by default; settings context.fileName accepts an ARRAY, e.g. ["AGENTS.md", "CONTEXT.md", "GEMINI.md"]
harnesses.instructionOrder: Global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md → configured workspace directories and their ancestors → just-in-time scan when a tool touches a file or directory. /memory show prints the concatenated text actually sent; /memory reload rescans.
harnesses.nonInteractive: -p / --prompt <string> (appended to stdin input if provided; forces non-interactive mode); -i / --prompt-interactive runs a prompt then stays interactive
harnesses.sessionStore: ~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/chats/ (project_hash derives from the project root). Retention keys general.sessionRetention.{enabled,maxAge,maxCount,minRetention}; turn cap model.maxSessionTurns.
harnesses.configFiles: user ~/.gemini/settings.json and workspace <project>/.gemini/settings.json — workspace overrides user
harnesses.pathGrant: --include-directories; folder trust via security.folderTrust.enabled with decisions stored in ~/.gemini/trustedFolders.json
gotchas: An untrusted folder's safe mode disables far more than file access: workspace settings are ignored, environment variables are ignored, extension management is limited, tool auto-acceptance is off, automatic memory loading is off, MCP servers do not connect, and custom commands do not load. A desk in an untrusted folder is not a degraded desk — it is a different environment.
Whether -p composes with -r/--resume for headless multi-turn is NOT documented; every official resume example is interactive.
harnesses.providerBind: Not surveyed. This row remains the deliberate warning row (see its other fields) rather than a recommendation.

caveats.why: Only ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json is documented; whether a project-level settings file exists, and whether allowNonWorkspaceAccess can be overridden per project or by flag, is unconfirmed — while extensions ARE workspace-local under .agents/.

Documentation names an onboarding prompt or /permissions; the config reference gives the projects.<path>.trust_level key. The non-interactive path for granting trust before a `codex exec` run is unclear, and an untrusted project silently drops the whole project-scoped layer.
A custom-provider mechanism exists, but the exact key set (base_url / env_key / wire_api and their spellings) was not read verbatim in this survey. Rule 1 keeps it out of the row.
The CLI-level newline-delimited JSON envelope is not specified; documentation gives only the SDK message shape, without stating that the CLI stdin contract is identical.
Only user and workspace scopes were confirmed; an OS-level system settings path was not found.
Confirmed absent rather than unconfirmed: print mode has no JSON or output-format option. Recorded as a caveat because it constrains which seats may run here, not because the fact is uncertain.

crossHarnessFacts.fact: Instruction-file discovery runs repository-root down to the working directory on every harness surveyed, and none exposes a setting, flag, or frontmatter field that reverses that order. The nearest-to-cwd file is merged LAST and therefore wins.
crossHarnessFacts.consequence: Charter specificity is obtained by PRECEDENCE (run the harness in the desk so the charter merges last), never by claiming a reversed load order. Corporate.md §2.2 is written against this fact.

crossHarnessFacts.fact: Instruction budgets are capped per harness, and the caps are small: one harness loads only the first 200 lines or 25 KB of its memory index, another stops accumulating instruction files at 32 KiB.
crossHarnessFacts.consequence: A charter competes with the project SSoT for a bounded budget. Charters stay short and point at paths (Corporate.md §6.3); a long charter silently truncates the thing it was supposed to override.

crossHarnessFacts.fact: At least one harness protects an agent's own configuration directories as read-only even inside otherwise-writable roots.
crossHarnessFacts.consequence: Corporate.md §9.2's no-self-configuration invariant has vendor precedent rather than being a house rule; harnesses without the protection need it enforced through the path grant and the charter.

crossHarnessFacts.fact: Pointing a harness at a non-first-party endpoint disables several of its own capabilities, some recoverable only via additional environment flags.
crossHarnessFacts.consequence: A custom endpoint is a capability trade, not a transparent substitution. A seat whose duty depends on a disabled capability must not be routed there — record the disabled set alongside any endpoint row.

crossHarnessFacts.fact: Turn and spend ceilings exist as per-invocation flags on at least one harness, and subagent spend aggregates into the parent's total.
crossHarnessFacts.consequence: Corporate.md §7.4b prefers binding the harness's own ceilings at spawn over implementing budget accounting in the module — a harness that can fail a spawn on breach is a stronger guarantee than module-side bookkeeping.

crossHarnessFacts.fact: A long-lived process holds the PATH snapshot it inherited at start. A harness installed — or self-updated into a new directory — after that moment is invisible to the process even though the user PATH in the registry carries it. Measured on the deployment host: three entries present in the user PATH and absent from the live IDE process, one of them the CLI that had just self-updated.
crossHarnessFacts.consequence: A desk launcher MUST resolve harness binaries by ABSOLUTE PATH (recorded per host in the roster) rather than relying on inherited PATH. A supervisor that shells out by bare command name will report a harness as missing that is in fact installed — and the failure looks like a configuration error rather than a stale environment.
confirmedBy: local measurement: HKCU:\Environment Path vs the live process PATH on the deployment host, 2026-07-25

crossHarnessFacts.fact: Whether an external API can staff a seat is decided by the harness, not by the API. Of the three harnesses measured here, one accepts arbitrary OpenAI-compatible endpoints through a declared provider (codex-cli, and only over the Responses wire), one accepts only its vendor plus three named clouds (claude-code), and one exposes no provider surface at all (agy). So "we have an API key" is never by itself an assignment: the question is which seats the key can reach, and the answer can be none.
crossHarnessFacts.why: A roster that assigns a model to a seat without checking the harness provider surface produces a seat that silently runs on the vendor default — the assignment appears in the chart and never happens in the process.
crossHarnessFacts.confirmedBy: local --help measurement (claude-code, codex-cli, agy) + web-sourced config semantics (codex-cli)

crossHarnessFacts.fact: A per-seat provider choice is only expressible if the harness honors provider config at a scope the seat controls. Codex honors model_provider / model_providers exclusively in the user-level config and ignores them in a project-local one (with a startup warning), so a Corporate desk — which is a directory, i.e. project-local — cannot carry its own provider. The per-seat mechanism there is a named profile layered per invocation, not a file in the desk.
crossHarnessFacts.why: Corporate §2 gives each seat a desk and expects desk-scoped configuration to be how a seat differs from its neighbours. Where the harness scopes a setting above the desk, that expectation silently fails to the user default, which is the same class as the §9.2 no-self-configuration invariant seen from the other side: the seat cannot configure itself even when it should.
crossHarnessFacts.confirmedBy: web-sourced 2026-07-26 (codex config reference + multiple provider-setup writeups); not verified against a live project-local override on this deployment

watchlist.item: Gemini CLI consumer-plan entitlement vs repository activity
watchlist.why: The official announcement states consumer-plan request serving stopped 2026-06-18, yet the repository was still being pushed to in late July and its README still advertises free-tier rate limits. Treat the announcement as authoritative for seat assignment and re-check whether the documentation catches up.
blocks: assigning any seat backed by a consumer Google subscription to gemini-cli rather than agy

watchlist.why: The prohibitions read from vendor terms are narrow and specific: credential sharing, offering consumer sign-in to third parties, and routing other parties' requests. They do not speak to how intensely a subscriber drives their own subscription through the vendor's own documented non-interactive mode — and every harness row above records such a mode as a published, maintained flag. §9.1 therefore requires the operator to DECLARE the lane and the fan-out ceiling rather than imposing a lane. Watch for terms revisions that would narrow the non-interactive surface itself, and record the clause verbatim if one appears.

A local OpenAI-compatible endpoint removes the entitlement question and the per-wake cost, which makes it the natural host for resident T4 seats — but capability is the trade. Confirm tool-calling, structured-output and context behaviour per serving stack and per model before a local seat is given work whose failure is not obvious.
blocks: assigning a local-lane seat any duty whose silent failure would not be caught

watchlist.why: A resident seat on a local model is only viable if the serving stack supports the tool-calling the harness requires. Confirm per serving stack and per model, not per family.
blocks: resident residency class on a local host (§7.1)

watchlist.why: A free API tier that trains on prompts is unusable for a private workspace regardless of its rate limits. Record the policy clause alongside any free-tier row, and keep the productionAllowed=false routing rule of §9.1 absolute.
blocks: routing any seat that reads project content to a free tier

watchlist.why: The CLI ships as a distributed binary with no source in its public repository. Version pinning and provenance checking therefore carry more weight here than for an open-source harness (§9.2).

watchlist.what: NVIDIA build.nvidia.com (NIM API catalog) free tier as a possible seat backer: 100+ hosted models (Nemotron, DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen, Mistral) behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, free through the Developer Program with no card.
watchlist.measuredClaims: Free rate limit reported as ~40 requests/minute (200 RPM by application). Signup grants ~1,000 inference credits, roughly one credit per call, with ~4,000 more attached to a 90-day AI Enterprise evaluation license. Production is priced per GPU-year. Numbers are WEB-SOURCED 2026-07-26 from secondary write-ups, not from an account of ours.
watchlist.blocking: Two unresolved items, either of which is disqualifying on its own. (1) DATA USE: public sources conflict — the NIM catalog terms are reported as not training on prompts and responses, while at least one write-up reads the privacy policy as recording inputs and outputs for training. Corporate §9.1 is deliberately asymmetric here: a free tier that may train on submitted content is never given a resident or production seat, so this must be resolved from the primary terms by the operator, not inferred. (2) WIRE: NIM is OpenAI chat/completions-shaped, and a codex custom provider now requires wire_api="responses" or it fails at startup — so even with the data question settled, the endpoint may not be reachable from the one harness here that accepts custom providers.
watchlist.verdict: Not an assignment candidate for any resident seat as of 2026-07-26. Plausible for burst / on-demand work on non-sensitive content IF the operator resolves the data-use question against the primary terms and a wire-compatible path exists. The credit budget (~5k calls total) is a trial resource, not a seat budget.
watchlist.confirmedBy: web-sourced secondary write-ups 2026-07-26; no account created, nothing measured against the live endpoint
